comparisons.peer_topic: 2025 Issuance of Series Z Preferred Stock
comparisons.peer_summary: In January 2025, the firm issued 76,000 shares of Series Z 6.85% Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock, which has a $25,000 liquidation preference, is redeemable at the firm's option starting February 10, 2030, and pays semi-annual dividends at 6.85% per annum until that date, thereafter resetting to 2.461% plus the five-year treasury rate.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures describe specific preferred stock series that are redeemable at the firm's option. MS discloses that its Series A and C shares are currently redeemable at the firm's option at any time. GS discloses that its newly issued Series Z preferred stock is redeemable at the firm's option, but with a specific deferral period, commencing February 10, 2030. This highlights a difference in the timing of redemption optionality: MS series are immediately redeemable, whereas GS Series Z is not redeemable until a future date.

sentences.text: 4.Series A and C are currently redeemable at the Firm's option, in whole or in part, from time to time.

Each share of Series Z Preferred Stock issued and outstanding has a liquidation preference of $25,000 per share, is represented by 25 depositary shares and is redeemable at the firm's option beginning February 10, 2030 at a redemption price equal to $25,000 per share plus declared and unpaid dividends.

JPM provides specific instances of exercising this right, redeeming multiple series of preferred stock (Series Q, R, S, U, FF, X, and HH) between April 2024 and February 2025. Both illustrate the firm's capacity to call preferred stock, with JPM detailing the volume and timing of recent redemptions.
